title: Medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex in approach-avoidance decisions (Starkweather et al., 2026): SEEG high-frequency activity, 6 patients (derivative)
description: This derivative dataset contains stereotactic EEG (SEEG) high-frequency activity (70-150 Hz) recorded from six patients with depth electrodes while they performed an approach-avoidance decision-making task. It accompanies a study of the differential contributions of medial and lateral orbitofrontal cortex to approach-avoidance decisions. The data are the authors' processed, trial-epoched HFA envelopes, repackaged in BIDS with behavioural variables, trial-quality flags and channel metadata.
methods_description: Patients with stereotactic depth electrodes (five at UCSF, one at WUSTL) performed an approach-avoidance task. SEEG signals were bipolar re-referenced, band-pass filtered at 0.5-200 Hz and notch filtered at 60 Hz and harmonics. HFA (70-150 Hz) was computed as the mean of ten 10-Hz sub-band Hilbert envelopes, each normalised to a 10 s pre-task baseline. Data were epoched per trial at 1 kHz and aligned to trial onset or decision.
